    "Given unequal group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505), use Type III sums of squares to account for imbalance",
    "Report effect sizes (eta-squared or partial eta-squared) for each ANOVA to quantify practical significance beyond statistical significance",
    "Check for heteroscedasticity given the wide range in Path Efficiency (max 29.8) and Time-to-Target (max 201.4) suggesting potential outliers"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [

    "If variance heterogeneity is present (likely given SD ranges), use Games-Howell post-hoc test which does not assume equal variances",
    "For Success (binary), use pairwise chi-square tests with Bonferroni correction or logistic regression contrasts with appropriate multiple comparison adjustment",
    "Focus post-hoc comparisons on theoretically meaningful contrasts: Combined vs single-modality conditions, sensory modalities vs Sham, and ICMS Only vs Visual conditions",
    "Report 95% confidence intervals for all pairwise differences to assess precision of estimates"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Control family-wise error rate across the 5 paradigms using the Benjamini-Hochberg FDR procedure for the 10 pairwise comparisons per variable, rather than Bonferroni, to maintain statistical power given the large sample size (n=76655). Apply this separately for each of the 5 response variables, acknowledging that this yields up to 50 total comparisons across the full analysis; consider a hierarchical approach where ANOVA must be significant before post-hoc testing is conducted.",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Given that Stim Paradigm is categorical and the goal is prediction, recommend a multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as the response variable and the five performance metrics as predictors. This directly models P(Stim Paradigm | performance) and yields interpretable log-odds ratios. Alternative: random forest or gradient boosting (XGBoost/LightGBM) for non-linear relationships, with 5-fold cross-validation stratified by Stim Paradigm to handle severe class imbalance (Combined: 63.7% vs Bright Visual Only: 4.3%). Do NOT use ordinary linear regression with dummy-coded Stim Paradigm as the response—this is inappropriate for categorical outcomes. If the research question permits, also consider linear discriminant analysis (LDA) or multinomial probit, but multinomial logistic regression is preferred for interpretability. Given the large n and class imbalance, use class weights or SMOTE during training, and report balanced accuracy, macro-averaged F1, and confusion matrix rather than raw accuracy.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assume satisfied given experimental design with distinct trials, though mouse-level clustering (8 mice) may violate this—consider mixed-effects models if mouse effects are substantial",
    "Normality: Assess via Shapiro-Wilk on residuals or Q-Q plots; given n=76655, central limit theorem applies but extreme outliers in Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target may distort variance estimates",
    "Homoscedasticity: Use Levene's test and Brown-Forsythe test; likely violated given 100-fold range in some variables—consider Welch's ANOVA or robust standard errors",
    "Multicollinearity among predictors: Check correlation matrix of performance variables before predictive modeling; Speed and Time-to-Target likely correlated",
    "Complete separation in logistic models: Check for cells with zero Success rates or perfect prediction by any variable",
    "Influence diagnostics: Identify trials with extreme Cook's distance or leverage, particularly given max values in Path Efficiency (29.8) and Time-to-Target (201.4)"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham condition will show significantly lower Success (0.27 vs 0.67-0.78), higher Time-to-Target (4.68s vs 2.56-3.14s), lower Path Efficiency (0.31 vs 0.43-0.50), lower Average Speed (10.74 vs 11.97-12.83), and lower AD (0.24 vs 0.34-0.40) based on summary statistics",
    "Combined stimulation will likely outperform or match single-modality conditions, with highest Success rate (0.78) and lowest Time-to-Target (2.56s)",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only will perform intermediately, with Dim Visual Only showing slightly lower Success (0.67) than ICMS Only (0.69) and higher Time-to-Target (3.14s vs 3.05s)",
    "Bright Visual Only will perform similarly to Combined, with Success 0.785 and Time-to-Target 2.61s, suggesting visual stimulation intensity matters",
    "AD (angular dispersion) will be highest in Combined (0.40) and Bright Visual Only (0.39), lowest in Sham (0.24), possibly reflecting more exploratory or distributed search patterns with effective stimulation",
    "Predictive model will likely achieve highest discrimination between Sham and active stimulation conditions, with poorest discrimination between Combined and Bright Visual Only due to similar performance profiles"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe class imbalance in Stim Paradigm (Combined 63.7% vs Bright Visual Only 4.3%) will bias predictive models toward majority class and complicate ANOVA power interpretation",
    "Mouse-level clustering unaccounted for in standard ANOVA: 8 mice with unequal trial counts (SC21LM 10986 vs SC11LM 7233) may introduce non-independence",
    "Success is binary but treated as continuous in summary; proper analysis requires logistic or mixed-effects logistic regression",
    "Extreme outliers in Path Efficiency (max 29.8) and Time-to-Target (max 201.4) suggest possible recording errors or aborted trials not excluded",
    "No information on trial sequence, learning effects, or session structure—temporal autocorrelation possible",
    "Single temperature setting (0.0) for LLM-based analysis may not generalize to other prompt configurations",
    "AD interpretation as angular dispersion is assumed from prompt; no validation of measurement method provided"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a mixed-effects model (linear for continuous outcomes, logistic for Success) with random intercepts for Mouse and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect, using lme4 or brms in R. For prediction, implement multinomial logistic regression with ridge/elastic net regularization to handle multicollinearity and class imbalance, using caret or glmnet. Report marginal means (emmeans) with Tukey-adjusted comparisons from the mixed model, and evaluate predictive performance with stratified cross-validation reporting per-class sensitivity/specificity. Additionally, explore non-linear relationships using generalized additive mixed models (GAMMs) for Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target given their skewed distributions."
}
